report:
# Research Findings: "Boiled Garlic Water Cures COVID-19"

**Conclusion: This claim is false.** There is no credible scientific evidence that boiled garlic water cures, treats, or prevents COVID-19.

## The Evidence

**No cure exists in reality.** As of current medical consensus, there is no home remedy that "cures" COVID-19; treatment relies on antiviral medications, supportive care, and vaccines developed and tested through rigorous clinical trials. The World Health Organization's official myth-busting resources explicitly address garlic, stating there is no evidence eating garlic protects people from the coronavirus, even though garlic is a healthy food with some general antimicrobial properties (https://www.who.int/emergencies/diseases/novel-coronavirus-2019/advice-for-public/myth-busters).

**Fact-checkers debunked it early and repeatedly.** This claim emerged in February 2020, at the very start of the pandemic, and was investigated by multiple independent fact-checking organizations. FactCheck.org found no scientific basis for garlic as a cure (https://www.factcheck.org/2020/02/fake-coronavirus-cures-part-2-garlic-isnt-a-cure/), and AFP Fact Check similarly concluded there's no proof that garlic-based tonics treat COVID-19 (https://factcheck.afp.com/theres-no-scientific-proof-tonic-onions-ginger-garlic-and-lemon-can-cure-covid-19).

**No legitimate clinical trials support it.** Searches for peer-reviewed research on garlic's antiviral efficacy against SARS-CoV-2 in humans turned up no controlled clinical trials demonstrating a curative or even significant therapeutic effect. Legitimate antiviral research for COVID-19 focused on drugs like remdesivir, monoclonal antibodies, and other pharmaceutical agents—not culinary remedies.

**Real-world harm occurred.** Belief in this myth had actual consequences: reports describe a woman in China hospitalized after consuming 1.5kg of raw garlic attempting to prevent infection (South China Morning Post: https://www.scmp.com/week-asia/health-environment/article/3049261/garlic-cant-keep-coronavirus-bay-neither-will).

## Bottom Line
While garlic has modest general health benefits, no scientific body or peer-reviewed study supports it as a COVID-19 cure. This is a well-documented pandemic-era myth, not an evidence-based treatment.
